item.title: Yellow River, China's mother river, runs clearer after decades of conservation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
ZHENGZHOU, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- The Hukou Waterfall on the Yellow River, once depicted on China's fourth-series 50-yuan banknotes as a torrent of muddy, turbulent water, now presents a markedly different scene, with its cascading waters running clear. Photographer Lyu Guiming, known for documenting the waterfall in Jixian County, Shanxi Province, since 1999, has witnessed the change. "Over the past decade, clear cascades at the waterfall have been my main photographic subject," Lyu said. "The contrast with the old scenes is striking." The changing waterscape reflects decades of efforts to protect and manage the Yellow River, China's second-longest river, which flows 5,464 km from its source in the highlands of Qinghai Province through nine provinces and autonomous regions, crossing deserts and loess lands before emptying into the Bohai Sea in Shandong Province, east China. In 1946, under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, an agency for people's Yellow River management was established on the river's banks in Heze, Shandong Province. Because Henan Province was frequently affected by flooding on the river, the Yellow River Conservancy Commission (YRCC) later moved its headquarters to Zhengzhou in December 1953. Thanks to 80 years of conservation efforts, the river, once prone to devastating floods, heavy sedimentation and shifting channels, now has cleaner waters and more sustainable water use. Historical records show that before the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, the river's lower reaches experienced more than 1,500 dyke breaches and overflows and changed course 26 times. Sediment was a persistent challenge, giving rise to the old saying that half of a bowl of Yellow River water is sand. Wei Xiangyang, the commission's chief engineer, outlined progress in flood control, a central part of river management. Dykes built to withstand major floods now stretch 1,371 km in total along the lower reaches. Forty flood-control reservoirs on the river and its tributaries have a combined flood-control capacity of 19 billion cubic meters. Over the past eight decades, these infrastructure projects have helped avoid an estimated 10.09 trillion yuan (around 1.5 trillion U.S. dollars) in economic losses from floods, Wei said. Efforts to curb soil erosion have also produced substantial results. Zhu Xiaoyong, director of the commission's soil and water conservation bureau, presented data showing that 290,500 square km of land affected by soil erosion across the river basin have been rehabilitated. Soil and water conservation measures have kept about 24.7 billion tonnes of sediment from entering the river. The Yellow River spans multiple regions and forms an integrated ecosystem that requires coordinated cross-regional management. "After years of research, we have developed a reservoir operation approach that stores clean water while discharging sediment," said Zhang Jinliang, chief scientist of Yellow River Engineering Consulting Co., Ltd. "Precision water-sediment regulation marks a shift from passive response to proactive action in managing the river." Water allocation has also achieved better coordination. Since a unified water-management system covering all provincial-level regions along the river was introduced in 1999, the Yellow River has flowed uninterrupted for 27 consecutive years. Over the years, more efficient water use has helped expand irrigated farmland in the river basin to 132 million mu (8.8 million hectares). The basin and downstream irrigation areas produce roughly 89.5 billion kilograms of grain annually, or 13.3 percent of China's national grain output. YRCC figures also show that water quality in the Yellow River Basin has markedly improved. The proportion of monitoring sections graded Class I to III, indicating good water quality, rose from 59.1 percent in 2016 to 93.2 percent in 2025. The changes are also visible in communities along the river. Lyu's photographs documenting the Hukou Waterfall's shifting waterscape have helped boost local tourism. His widely shared photos have helped turn tourism into a pillar industry in a county that was once impoverished. "The Yellow River ecosystem forms an integrated whole," he said. "From headwater conservation in the upper reaches and soil and water conservation in the middle reaches to wetland restoration in the lower reaches, green has become a defining feature of high-quality development in the Yellow River Basin." ■

item.title: China Focus: UN official says world can learn from China's urban renewal experience
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
FUZHOU, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Valuable lessons for global urban development can be drawn from China's people-centered approach to urban renewal, Anacláudia Rossbach, United Nations under-secretary-general and executive director of UN-Habitat, said during the Global Observance of World Cities Day in China's Fuzhou. Under the theme "Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All," the activities in Fuzhou, capital of east China's Fujian Province, brought together city leaders, planners and other stakeholders to discuss global housing challenges from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2. UN-Habitat's World Cities Report 2026 estimates that up to 3.4 billion people lack access to secure, safe and adequate housing, including more than 1 billion people living in informal settlements and slums. Rossbach called for scaling up inclusive urban regeneration efforts to address this crisis. Describing China's urban transformation experience as "fantastic," Rossbach said the country's approach to urban development offers valuable lessons, particularly in its growing emphasis on people-centered, neighborhood-level solutions. Rossbach also pointed to China's efforts to balance cultural heritage preservation with modernization. "In Chinese cities, they all work together in a very balanced way," she noted. This approach is reflected in Jingdezhen, China's "porcelain capital." Located in Jiangxi Province in the country's east, it was among five cities honored with the fourth-cycle Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities (Shanghai Award). Jingdezhen has combined the preservation of its centuries-old ceramic heritage with inclusive neighborhood renewal, improvements to older residential areas and expanded public services. The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites, notably, were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026. China has set a target of renovating 1,500 old streets and factory compounds from 2026 to 2030, bringing in new industries and business models to inject fresh momentum into urban development. During her visit to Fuzhou, Rossbach toured a regenerated old town quarter where historic buildings have been preserved and new buildings have been designed in traditional architectural styles. She was impressed by the bustling street life and the local application of the "proximity" concept, which clusters services, commercial outlets and public transport links for residents' convenience. Rossbach also highlighted China's attention to vulnerable groups in urban renewal, such as children, older people and persons with disabilities. She recalled seeing elderly residents practicing tai chi and children playing in public spaces during an earlier visit to Beijing. Under the national urban renewal plan (2026-2030) released earlier this year, China aims to launch renovations of 115,000 old urban residential compounds, retrofit or install 575,000 residential elevators, and build or upgrade 50,000 hectares of urban green space. "The solution is not just building houses. It's not enough. This is the main lesson that we learned from China. You have to create the conditions for people to live together," said the UN-Habitat chief. Adequate housing, she explained, involves not only affordability and accessibility but also good connectivity to urban infrastructure, cultural adequacy and climate resilience. "We learned from many examples, including here in Fuzhou, how important it is to work with communities to understand what their vision for the city is, what their aspirations and expectations are, so that they can be reflected in city planning and housing policies," Rossbach added. The three-day event was jointly organized by China's Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian provincial government and UN-Habitat. ■

item.title: Xi, Peruvian president exchange congratulations on 55th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Noting that China and Peru are comprehensive strategic partners, Xi said bilateral relations have withstood changes in the international landscape and maintained sound development momentum over the past 55 years. Political mutual trust between the two countries has grown stronger, practical cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results, and friendship between the two peoples has taken deep root, Xi said, noting that China appreciates Peru's consistent adherence to the one-China principle. The protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement took effect on Sunday. It is believed that it will give a strong boost to the upgrade of the China-Peru economic and trade cooperation, and will inject fresh impetus into the development of bilateral relations, Xi said. Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Peru ties, and stands ready to work with President Fujimori to take the 55th anniversary of ties as a new starting point to steer bilateral relations to new heights for the greater benefits of the two peoples. Fujimori, for her part, said that Peru and China have jointly forged a robust bond featuring friendship, mutual respect and cooperation. Bilateral relations have continuously drawn strength from the traditional friendship between the two peoples, and have deepened and expanded within the framework of the comprehensive strategic partnership, she said. Fujimori said the Peruvian side reaffirmed its firm commitment to the one-China principle and stands ready to continue strengthening political dialogue and cooperation with China. ■

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. item.title: Xi stresses improving protection, coordination to make Yellow River more beautiful
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has stressed efforts to continuously improve protection and coordination to make the Yellow River more beautiful. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on further advancing the protection and governance of the Yellow River. Xi emphasized that solid efforts must be made to promote ecological protection and high-quality development in the Yellow River Basin, carry forward the Yellow River culture, and ensure that this mother river delivers sustainable benefits to the Chinese nation and future generations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a work conference on comprehensively advancing the protection and governance of the Yellow River, held on Monday in Zhengzhou, central China's Henan Province. Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the conference. He called for joint efforts to advance greater protection and coordinated governance of the Yellow River, ensure the river is well managed, and enhance the conservation and intensive utilization of water resources. The conference briefed participants on the achievements in Yellow River governance over the past 80 years under the leadership of the CPC. Thanks to 80 years of conservation efforts, the river, once prone to devastating floods, heavy sedimentation and shifting channels, now has cleaner waters and more sustainable water use. The Yellow River, China's second-longest river, flows 5,464 km through nine provinces and autonomous regions, crossing deserts and loess lands, before emptying into the Bohai Sea in Shandong. ■
